key_insight: Non-dimensionalization can determine PINN trainability: free-fall scaling avoids the large buoyancy coefficient associated with severe gradient imbalance under thermal-diffusive scaling.
engineering_relevance: Choosing physically appropriate scaling before training can improve PINN reliability for buoyancy-driven heat-transfer prediction.
method: Compare thermal-diffusive and free-fall scalings under identical training conditions.
Evaluate a differentially heated square cavity at Pr = 0.71 and Ra = 10³–10⁵.
Measure loss gradients and test sparse-data supervision and adaptive loss weighting.
evidence_signal: For Ra ≤ 10⁴, free-fall scaling yielded mean Nusselt-number errors below 1.1%, versus 157–650% for diffusive scaling, which diverged at Ra = 10⁵.
watch_item: Free-fall scaling did not eliminate all failures: the unsteady PINN captured long-time heat transfer but missed the transient Nusselt-number overshoot.
paper_title: Inherent Failure Modes of Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Buoyancy-Driven Flow: Role of Non-Dimensionalization in Network Training
